extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists, and fact-checkers tracking/discussing fake news websites
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia list/catalog of miscellaneous fake-news websites (those that don't fit other specialized fake-news lists), with notes on why each site is classified as fake/misleading and source citations. Used to identify, document, and research disinformation outlets and networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion as 'miscellaneous' fake news websites
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a list of miscellaneous fake news websites that do not fit into any of the other fake news website lists such as lists of campaigns by individuals, corporate disinformation campaigns, fraudulent fact-checking websites, generative-AI-based fake sites, hate group–sponsored fake news, satirical fake news websites, troll farm websites, user-generated fake news websites, and other online networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites eligible for this list are those that are identified as fake/misleading but are not already categorized under the other specialized lists. Inclusion should be supported by citations to reliable sources (e.g., PolitiFact, FactCheck.org, Snopes, Lead Stories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for reliable-source citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The article requests help: add missing items with references to reliable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should be accompanied by references to reliable fact-checking outlets, news reports, or research documenting the site's deceptive behavior; unsourced additions are discouraged. The page is a dynamic list and may never be exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impostor sites / imitation of legitimate outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Many entries are labelled as 'Impostor site' or 'Imitates' (e.g., 'Impostor site, per PolitiFact'; 'Imitates The Boston Globe'; 'Imitates BBC' or 'Imitates USA Network').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impostor classification is applied when a site copies or mimics the branding, domain style, or presentation of a reputable outlet in order to deceive readers. Examples: domain lookalikes (nytimespost.com), near-duplicate branding, or plagiarized content presented as original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spoof / parody republished without disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sites are described as 'Spoof of [legitimate outlet]' or 'Reposted article from satirical site... without satirical disclaimer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that republish satirical content or intentionally spoof legitimate publications but present the material as factual (or omit disclaimers) are treated as sources of misinformation for this list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and copying of established outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries note when sites 'plagiarize CNBC stories' or 'republished a hoax' or 'copied story from The Last Line of Defense' or 'plagiarized article by the Los Angeles Times.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism of legitimate news content, sometimes with altered headlines or false context, is grounds for listing; notes usually include the original source and citation showing the copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing fabricated quotes and manipulated attributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entries cite 'fabricated celebrity quote', 'manipulated and misattributed celebrity quote', or fabricated attributions to organizations (e.g., Human Rights Watch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that invent quotes, attribute statements that were never made, or otherwise fabricate sources are marked as fake; fact-check citations document the fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing false events / hoaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites are described as having 'published a false news story' (e.g., fake election results, fake celebrity deaths, false claims about public figures) or 'published hoax on missing child.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of fabricated events or hoaxes that have been debunked by reputable fact-checkers are recorded with citations and brief notes about the false claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misinformation on public health (anti-vaccine, COVID-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several entries explicitly 'Spread COVID-19 vaccine conspiracy theories', 'Spread anti-vaccine misinformation', or 'Published false claims about COVID-19 vaccinations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that propagate health-related misinformation (vaccines, cures, pandemics) are identified and linked to the specific false claims and fact-checking sources documenting harms or inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of conspiracy theories and extremist content
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sites are characterized as promoting 'QAnon', 'Holocaust denial', 'conspiracy theories', or being 'far-right' outlets that promote disinformation and extremist narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification includes documentation of the conspiratorial or extremist narratives promoted, with sources showing repeated dissemination of such content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of manipulated or out-of-context images
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries note 'published false story with a Photoshopped image as evidence' or 'published a false story with an out-of-context image.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When images are fabricated, doctored, or shown out-of-context to mislead readers, the site is documented with citations that explain the image manipulation and correct context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain tricks: IDN homograph attacks and lookalike domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include use of 'lookalike letters from other scripts' (IDN homograph attacks) to spoof legitimate station websites and deceptive domain names that imitate real outlets (e.g., ΚΒΟΙ2.com).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites using character substitution, lookalike domains, or other domain-engineering techniques to impersonate legit sources are flagged; notes explain the technique and purpose (deception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared infrastructure or network indicators (same IP / AdSense)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sites are noted as having the 'same IP address as conservativedaily.info' or 'Has the same Google AdSense account as conservativedaily.info'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical linkage (shared IPs, ad accounts, registration details) is used to identify networks of related fake sites; such network evidence is recorded and cited when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing other fake outlets' content (circular/chain copying)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many entries say 'Copied story from The Last Line of Defense', 'Republished a hoax from World News Daily Report', or 'Copied article from [satirical or fake site]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list tracks propagation chains where sites repeatedly republish the same fabricated stories, showing how false content circulates across multiple domains; entries cite the originating fake source when known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging/verification by independent fact-checkers and watchdogs
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple entries reference being labelled by PolitiFact, FactCheck.org, Snopes, Lead Stories, NewsGuard, Africa Check, or being debunked in news reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion and classification often rely on determinations by established fact-checking organizations; citations to those organizations are the primary evidence used on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization and malicious economic incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include networks monetizing via ad revenue, scams, or issuing false reports that impacted markets (e.g., Bloomberg.market false takeover report that caused an 8% spike).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites created primarily to earn ad revenue, scam readers, or manipulate markets by publishing fabricated business/financial news are documented with the economic motive and effects when reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of anonymity, fake ownership, or front organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries mention sites' opaque ownership, ties to actors (e.g., Macedonian networks), or being 'owned by' persons tied to other misinformation outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative reporting linking sites to owners, operators, or cross-site personnel is used to classify and describe the provenance and coordinated behavior of fake-news networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing real and fake content to evade moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sites 'mix real news along with its fake news in an attempt to circumvent Facebook's crackdown on them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that intersperse legitimate reporting with fabricated stories to appear credible or avoid platform moderation are documented; descriptions note the tactic and cite platform or news investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate deception with fabricated official documents/letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include 'Fabricated a letter from the British Ministry of Defense' or 'fabricated attribution to an organization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites that create bogus documents or fake official communications to back false claims are flagged; entries include fact-check citations demonstrating falsification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malicious technical behavior (phishing, malware flags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sites are marked as 'flagged by Google as potential phishing site' or noted for spreading malware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When technical abuse (phishing, malware distribution) accompanies misinformation, the site is listed with notes and sources that document the security threats or platform warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable public impact as evidence (e.g., widely shared, retweeted, or cited by politicians)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page notes when fake stories were 'shared by' public figures, 'tweeted by the president', or otherwise had outsized public/political impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-impact dissemination (amplification by politicians or large audiences) is recorded to document harm and reach; fact-checks and news reports are cited as evidence.
